description: The date and time when the production order was formally released to the shop floor for execution. Release triggers material staging, capacity reservation, and MES order activation. Maps to SAP PP order release date/time.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module; Apriso/Dassault MES; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5

description: The quantity of units that required rework (non-conforming units corrected and returned to production flow) during execution of this order. Distinct from scrap — reworked units are salvaged. Used for quality cost analysis and APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM Module; IATF 16949 Clause 8.7; APQP

description: The quantity of units scrapped or rejected during production of this order due to quality defects or process failures. Used for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate calculation, scrap cost analysis, and FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/QM Module; IATF 16949 Clause 8.7; SPC

description: Indicates whether this production order is part of the SOP (Start of Production) launch phase for a new vehicle program. True = SOP launch order subject to enhanced quality monitoring and APQP controls; False = regular series production order.

The planned standard cost to produce the target quantity under this order, calculated from the BOM (Bill of Materials) component costs and routing activity rates in SAP CO (Controlling). Expressed in the plant's local currency. Used for cost variance analysis and EBITDA reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; IATF 16949 Clause 9.1; GAAP/IFRS

description: The planned quantity of vehicles or sub-assemblies to be produced under this order, expressed in the base unit of measure (typically 'EA' for each). Maps to SAP PP planned order quantity (GAMNG). Used for capacity planning and production scheduling.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5

description: The date and time when the production order was set to Technically Completed (TECO) status in SAP PP, indicating all manufacturing operations are finished and the order is pending cost settlement. Distinct from actual_finish_timestamp which records the last physical operation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/CO Module; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5

description: The base unit of measure for the target and confirmed quantities on this production order (e.g., EA = Each for vehicles, PC = Piece for components, SET for kits, KG for bulk materials). Maps to SAP base unit of measure (MEINS).

The last VIN (Vehicle Identification Number) in the sequential range assigned to units produced under this order. Together with vin_range_start, defines the complete set of vehicles traceable to this production order for recall, warranty, and homologation purposes.
reference: ISO 3779; NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565; SAE J272

description: The first VIN (Vehicle Identification Number) in the sequential range assigned to units produced under this order. VINs are 17-character alphanumeric identifiers conforming to ISO 3779. Used for build traceability, recall management, and regulatory reporting to NHTSA.
reference: ISO 3779; NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565; SAE J272

description: Indicates whether WIP (Work in Progress) costs have been calculated and posted to the financial ledger for this production order in the current period. True = WIP posted; False = WIP not yet posted. Used for period-end financial closing in SAP CO.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; GAAP/IFRS IAS 2

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the master production schedule (MPS) record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: REQUIRED: Production schedules are often filtered by nameplate; nameplate‑level planning dashboards need this FK.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where the scheduled production will occur. Corresponds to the SAP Plant organizational unit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Org Structure; IATF 16949

description: Reference to the specific production line (e.g., final assembly, body shop, paint shop, stamping) within the plant where the scheduled build will take place.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Work Center; Apriso/Dassault MES

description: Reference to the vehicle model (e.g., sedan, SUV, truck, EV) being scheduled for production. Links to the vehicle master product record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Foreign key linking to engineering.vehicle_program. Business justification: Production schedules are generated per vehicle program; schedule analytics filter by vehicle_program_id.
Actual number of vehicles produced and confirmed as good units by the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) during the schedule period. Populated upon schedule completion from Apriso/Dassault MES.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES; SAP S/4HANA PP Goods Receipt; IATF 16949 Clause 9.1

description: Name or employee identifier of the production planning manager who formally approved this schedule version for release to the shop floor. Required for IATF 16949 document control and audit trail.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5; SAP S/4HANA PP Workflow

description: Timestamp when the production schedule was formally approved for release. Marks the transition from 'draft' to 'released' status and triggers supplier call-off generation.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5; SAP S/4HANA PP Workflow

description: Manufacturing process stage covered by this schedule record. Reflects the major shop areas in automotive assembly: stamping (metal forming), body shop (welding/joining), paint (surface treatment), final assembly (powertrain/trim installation), or trim-chassis-final (TCF integrated line).
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES; SAP S/4HANA PP Routing; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5

description: Total available production capacity in hours for this schedule period on the assigned production line, accounting for planned downtime, maintenance windows, and shift patterns.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Capacity Planning; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Body style classification of the vehicles scheduled for production. Used for production line configuration, tooling setup, and capacity planning by body type.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Classification; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Ending sequence number for the JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build order within this schedule period. Together with build_sequence_start defines the range of vehicle sequence numbers assigned to this schedule.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES; JIS Standard; SAP S/4HANA PP Sequencing

description: Starting sequence number for the JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build order within this schedule period. Used by MES and AGV systems to sequence vehicle bodies through the production line in the correct order.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES; JIS Standard; SAP S/4HANA PP Sequencing

description: Classification of the production build type. 'standard' = full series production; 'ckd' = Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kit assembly; 'skd' = Semi Knocked Down (SKD) assembly; 'pilot' = pre-production pilot build; 'pre_series' = pre-series validation build.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP; Siemens Teamcenter PLM; APQP Phase 4-5; IATF 16949

description: Timestamp when supplier delivery call-offs were transmitted to the supply base for this production schedule. Used for OTD (On-Time Delivery) tracking and supplier performance measurement.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Scheduling Agreement; IATF 16949 Clause 8.4; JIT Standard

description: Planned capacity utilization percentage for this schedule period, calculated as (confirmed_quantity × takt_time) / available_capacity_hours × 100. Stored as a planning input from SAP PP capacity leveling, not a derived KPI.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Capacity Leveling; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Number of vehicles confirmed for production after capacity leveling, constraint resolution, and production planning approval. May differ from planned_quantity due to capacity constraints or material availability.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Capacity Planning; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Timestamp when this production schedule record was first created in the system, either by an MRP run or manual entry. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.
Official End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle model/model year. Schedules beyond this date are invalid. Used for phase-out planning, last-time-buy procurement, and regulatory deregistration.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP; Siemens Teamcenter PLM; NHTSA Homologation

description: Fiscal period (month number 1-12 or 1-16 for special periods) within the fiscal year. Enables alignment of production volumes with financial reporting periods for management accounting and EBITDA analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-CO Fiscal Period; GAAP/IFRS

description: Fiscal year (FY) to which this production schedule belongs. Used for financial planning, CapEx allocation, and EBITDA reporting alignment between production volumes and financial periods.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-CO Fiscal Year; GAAP/IFRS Financial Reporting

description: Date up to which the production schedule is frozen and cannot be changed without formal change control. Protects supplier call-offs and JIT/JIS delivery commitments within the frozen window.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Planning Time Fence; IATF 16949 Clause 8.4; JIT/JIS Standard

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this schedule record is currently within the freeze horizon and locked against changes. True = frozen (no modifications allowed without change control); False = open for revision.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Planning Time Fence; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this production schedule record. Updated on every revision, status change, or quantity adjustment. Essential for incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.

The automotive model year (MY) designation for the vehicles being scheduled. Used for regulatory compliance (CAFE, EPA), BOM versioning, and sales planning. Typically one year ahead of the calendar year for SOP planning.
reference: NHTSA FMVSS; EPA CAFE Standards; SAE International MY Definition

description: Total number of vehicles planned for production in this schedule period as determined by the MRP run. Represents the gross requirement before capacity and constraint adjustments.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP-MRP Planned Order Quantity; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Powertrain technology classification for the vehicles in this schedule. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine; HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle; PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle; EV = Battery Electric Vehicle; FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Drives regulatory reporting (CAFE, EPA, CARB) and BOM variant selection.
reference: EPA CAFE Standards; CARB ZEV Mandate; NHTSA FMVSS; SAE J1711

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the primary regulatory market for which these vehicles are being produced. Determines applicable homologation standards (NHTSA/FMVSS for USA, UNECE for Europe, etc.), emissions certification (EPA, CARB, Euro 6), and CAFE compliance tracking. reference: NHTSA FMVSS; EPA Emissions Standards; UNECE Vehicle Regulations; CARB; ISO 3166-1

description: Business reason code or description for the most recent schedule revision. Examples: material shortage, capacity constraint, demand change, quality hold, tooling failure, model mix adjustment. Required for change control audit trail per IATF 16949.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 (Document Control); SAP S/4HANA PP Change Management

description: The principal planned production date (or start date of the weekly/monthly bucket) for this schedule record. Represents the real-world business event date when production is planned to occur.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Planned Order; IATF 16949

description: End date of the production schedule period. For daily schedules this equals schedule_date; for weekly/monthly buckets this marks the last day of the planning period.

Free-text field for production planners to record contextual notes, exceptions, or special instructions associated with this schedule record. Examples: tooling changeover notes, quality hold references, special customer order constraints.

Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the production schedule record, sourced from SAP PP (Production Planning). Used for cross-system reference and communication with supply chain and manufacturing teams.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Current lifecycle state of the production schedule record. 'draft' = initial planning; 'released' = approved for execution; 'frozen' = within freeze horizon, no changes allowed; 'in_execution' = active shop floor production; 'completed' = all planned units built; 'cancelled' = schedule voided.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1; Apriso/Dassault MES

description: Time granularity of the production schedule record. 'daily' = day-level MPS; 'weekly' = weekly bucket plan; 'monthly' = monthly capacity plan. Determines the planning horizon and supplier call-off frequency.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP-MRP Planning Horizon; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Incremental version number of the production schedule. Each MRP (Material Requirements Planning) run or manual revision increments this counter, enabling version comparison and rollback analysis.
Precise timestamp when production is scheduled to complete for this schedule record. Used for shift planning, takt time validation, and downstream logistics coordination.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Work Order Scheduling; Apriso/Dassault MES

description: Precise timestamp when production is scheduled to begin on the line for this schedule record. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing, AGV routing, and supplier call-off timing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Work Order Scheduling; Apriso/Dassault MES; JIS Standard

description: Shift configuration planned for this production schedule period. Determines available production hours and workforce requirements. Single = 1 shift/day; Double = 2 shifts/day; Triple = 3 shifts/day; Weekend = weekend-only production.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Capacity Planning; SuccessFactors Workforce Planning

description: Official Start of Production (SOP) date for the vehicle model/model year being scheduled. Marks the formal launch of series production. Used to validate that schedule dates fall within the active production window.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP; Siemens Teamcenter PLM Program Management; APQP Phase 5

description: Boolean flag indicating whether supplier delivery call-offs (JIT/JIS delivery schedules) have been generated and transmitted to suppliers based on this production schedule. True = call-offs sent; False = pending call-off generation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Scheduling Agreement; JIT/JIS Standard; IATF 16949 Clause 8.4

description: Planned takt time in seconds per vehicle unit for this production schedule. Takt time = available production time divided by customer demand rate. Drives line balancing, AGV pacing, and JIS sequencing intervals.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Rate Routing; Apriso/Dassault MES; SAE Manufacturing Standards

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the rework order record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7 - Control of Nonconforming Outputs

description: Foreign key linking to customer.case. Business justification: Warranty and quality processes require traceability from a customer complaint case to the shop-floor rework order it triggered. Quality engineers and warranty analysts use this link to measure case-to

Foreign key linking to engineering.change. Business justification: Rework orders are frequently initiated by engineering change orders requiring retrofit of in-process or built vehicles (e.g., a safety-related ECO mandating rework of VINs in a range). This FK enables
Reference to the quality defect record in the quality domain that triggered this rework order. Links rework traceability to the originating inspection finding or defect notification.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Defect Record

description: Foreign key linking to quality.inspection_lot. Business justification: Closed-loop quality process: an inspection lot rejection triggers a rework order. Linking rework_order to the originating inspection_lot enables inspection-to-rework cycle tracking, re-inspection clos
Reference to the manufacturing plant where the rework operation is being executed. Aligns with SAP Plant (Werk) organizational unit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Organizational Structure; IATF 16949 Section 4.1

Reference to the originating production order from which this rework order was raised. Links the rework event back to the scheduled manufacturing work order in SAP PP or MES.
reference: SAP PP Production Order; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1

Foreign key linking to inventory.sku_master. Business justification: Rework orders in automotive manufacturing consume replacement components (SKUs) for defect repair. Linking to sku_master supports rework material cost tracking, parts reservation against rework orders

Foreign key linking to manufacturing.vehicle_build. Business justification: rework_order has a denormalized vin STRING attribute that identifies the vehicle being reworked. vehicle_build is the authoritative record for a vehicle unit on the shop floor, keyed by VIN. Adding ve

Foreign key linking to vehicle.vin_registry. Business justification: IATF 16949 and NHTSA recall investigations require direct VIN-to-rework traceability. Rework orders must be traceable to the specific VIN for regulatory compliance and warranty root-cause analysis. ve

Foreign key linking to aftersales.aftersales_warranty_claim. Business justification: Warranty-driven manufacturing rework (field-return defects triggering production rework) must reference the originating warranty claim for supplier recovery, warranty cost chargeback, and IATF correct
Reference to the work center or repair station assigned to execute the rework operation. Corresponds to SAP PP Work Center or MES work station definition.
reference: SAP PP Work Center; Apriso/Dassault MES Work Station

description: Actual date and time when the rework operation was completed and the unit was released for re-inspection or returned to the production line. Recorded by MES upon order closure.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Time Tracking; SAP PM Order Confirmation

description: Actual labor hours consumed to complete the rework operation, recorded upon order completion in MES or SAP PM. Compared against planned hours for efficiency analysis and cost variance reporting.
reference: SAP PM Actual Costs; Apriso/Dassault MES Time Tracking; IATF 16949 Section 9.1

description: Actual date and time when the rework technician began executing the rework operation, as recorded by MES shop floor data collection or operator confirmation.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Time Tracking; SAP PM Order Confirmation

description: Code representing the specific assembly stage or station within the production line where the nonconformance was detected (e.g., body framing, paint primer, trim line, chassis marriage). Supports JIS (Just-in-Sequence) traceability.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Station Configuration; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.2

description: The BOM (Bill of Materials) component or part number of the specific sub-assembly or component requiring rework. References the engineering BOM managed in Siemens Teamcenter or SAP MM.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM BOM Management; SAP MM Material Master; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1

description: Reference number or identifier of the corrective action (CAR) or 8D problem-solving report raised in response to this rework event. Links the rework order to the formal quality improvement process.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 10.2.1 - Corrective Action; SAP QM Corrective Action; APQP 8D Report

description: Date and time when the rework order record was first created in the source system (MES or SAP QM). Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance purposes.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 7.5 - Documented Information; ISO 9001:2015 Section 7.5

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary cost fields on this rework order (rework_labor_cost, rework_material_cost). Typically the plant's local operating currency (e.g., USD, EUR, MXN).
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP FI Currency Configuration

description: Standardized defect classification code identifying the type of nonconformance that triggered the rework order. Aligns with the plant defect code catalogue maintained in SAP QM or MES quality module.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Defect Code Catalogue

description: Free-text narrative description of the defect or nonconformance identified during in-process quality inspection that initiated this rework order. Captured by the quality inspector or MES operator.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Notification Long Text

description: Standardized code identifying the physical location or zone on the vehicle or sub-assembly where the defect was found (e.g., body zone, paint zone, chassis area). Used for spatial defect analysis and NVH (Noise Vibration Harshness) correlation.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; Euro NCAP Defect Zone Classification

description: Code indicating the method by which the defect was detected prior to rework order creation (e.g., visual inspection, automated gauge check, functional test, quality audit, customer feedback). Supports FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) detection ranking analysis.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; FMEA Detection Ranking; SAP QM Inspection Method

description: Date and time when the nonconformance was originally detected during in-process quality inspection, triggering the creation of this rework order. The principal business event timestamp for this transaction.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; SAP QM Inspection Lot Creation Date; Apriso MES Quality Event

description: Final disposition decision for the nonconforming unit after rework evaluation. Repaired indicates successful correction; scrapped indicates the unit is unrecoverable; concession (use-as-is) indicates acceptance of the nonconformance with documented deviation; return to supplier applies to purchased components.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1 - Disposition of Nonconforming Product; ISO 9001:2015 Section 8.7

description: Code identifying the specific quality inspection checkpoint or gate (e.g., body-in-white audit, paint final audit, end-of-line check) at which the defect was detected and the rework order was initiated.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; SAP QM Inspection Lot; Apriso MES Quality Gate

description: Indicates whether the vehicle or sub-assembly is placed on a regulatory hold pending rework completion and re-inspection. A regulatory hold prevents the unit from advancing to the next production stage or shipping.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 573; CARB Compliance; DOT FMVSS; IATF 16949 Section 8.7

description: Indicates whether the defect triggering this rework order is classified as safety-critical, requiring escalation per NHTSA, DOT, or internal safety reporting protocols. Safety-related rework orders may trigger FMEA review and potential field action assessment.

description: Indicates whether this rework event caused a production line stoppage (Andon pull or line stop). Used for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) impact analysis and production downtime reporting.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1; Apriso/Dassault MES Andon Event; SAP PP Downtime Recording

description: The vehicle model year (MY) of the unit undergoing rework. Used for regulatory compliance reporting, warranty analysis, and production quality trending by model year.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565; SAP PP Production Version

description: Scheduled date and time when the rework operation is planned to be completed. Used to calculate planned rework cycle time and assess impact on downstream production sequencing.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Scheduling; SAP PP Scheduling

description: Estimated labor hours planned to complete the rework operation, as defined in the rework routing or standard repair time (SRT) catalogue. Used for capacity planning and cost estimation.
reference: SAP PP Routing Standard Values; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1

description: Scheduled date and time when the rework operation is planned to begin, as determined by the MES scheduler or production planner. Used for shop floor capacity planning and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Scheduling; SAP PP Scheduling

description: Business priority assigned to the rework order to drive scheduling and resource allocation on the shop floor. Critical priority typically indicates a safety-related or regulatory nonconformance requiring immediate resolution.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Notification Priority

description: Indicates whether a formal re-inspection is required after rework completion before the unit can be released to the next production stage or shipped. Mandatory for safety-related or regulatory nonconformances.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1; SAP QM Re-Inspection Trigger

description: Outcome of the quality re-inspection performed after rework completion. Pass indicates the unit meets specification; fail triggers a secondary rework or scrap decision; conditional pass indicates acceptance with documented deviation.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; SAP QM Usage Decision; Apriso MES Quality Gate Result

description: Number of rework attempts made on this unit or component for the same defect. Multiple rework attempts on the same unit indicate a chronic quality issue and may trigger escalation or scrap decision per quality policy.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1; SAP QM Notification Recurrence

description: Document number or reference to the approved rework instruction, repair standard, or Technical Service Bulletin (TSB) that governs the rework procedure. Ensures traceability to authorized repair methods.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1; SAP DMS Document Reference; Siemens Teamcenter Document Management

description: Total internal labor cost incurred for the rework operation, calculated from actual rework hours and the applicable labor rate. Expressed in the plant's operating currency. Used for quality cost (Cost of Poor Quality - COPQ) reporting.
reference: SAP CO Cost Object Controlling; IATF 16949 Section 9.1; APQP Cost of Poor Quality

description: Cost of replacement parts and materials consumed during the rework operation. Sourced from SAP MM goods issue postings against the rework order. Contributes to total Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) calculation.

description: Actual date and time when the vehicle build was completed at the final assembly stage and signed off for PDI (Pre-Delivery Inspection). Null if the build is still in progress. Used for cycle time, throughput, and SOP/EOP milestone tracking.

description: The Just-in-Sequence (JIS) production sequence number assigned to this vehicle on the assembly line. Determines the order in which vehicles are built and parts are delivered to the line. Critical for JIS/JIT supply chain synchronization.

description: Actual date and time when the vehicle build process commenced at the first production stage (typically body-in-white or stamping entry). Principal business event timestamp for the build lifecycle. Used for cycle time calculation and OTD (On-Time Delivery) analysis.

description: Current lifecycle status of the vehicle build record. Drives shop floor workflow, MES gating, and production reporting. 'on_hold' indicates a quality or material hold; 'rework' indicates a defect requiring corrective action before completion.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES – Work Order Status; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.2

description: Classification of the vehicle build type: standard (full local assembly), CKD (Completely Knocked Down – assembled from imported kits), SKD (Semi Knocked Down), pilot (pre-SOP trial build), or prototype (engineering validation). Affects BOM, duty classification, and regulatory reporting.

description: Actual timestamp when the chassis assembly stage was completed. Null if stage not yet completed.

description: Actual timestamp when the vehicle entered the chassis assembly stage for powertrain marriage, suspension, and drivetrain installation.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES – Stage Tracking; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1

description: Timestamp when this vehicle build record was first created in the MES/data platform. Represents the audit trail creation event, distinct from the build_start_timestamp which is the actual shop floor event time.

description: Actual timestamp when the vehicle entered the final assembly stage for fluids, wheels, glass, and end-of-line checks.

description: Coded reason for the production hold applied to this vehicle build (e.g., QUALITY_DEFECT, MISSING_PART, ECN_CHANGE, SAFETY_CONCERN). Null if hold_flag is False. description: The target regulatory market for which this vehicle is homologated and built (e.g., USA, DEU, GBR, CHN, AUS). Determines applicable safety, emissions, and labeling standards. Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes.

description: The automotive model year (MY) designation for the vehicle being built (e.g., 2025). Determines applicable regulatory standards, BOM revision, and homologation requirements. Distinct from the calendar year of production.

description: The manufacturer's paint color code applied to this vehicle during the paint stage (e.g., G1W – Super White, 040 – Classic White). Used for paint shop scheduling, color sequencing optimization, and customer order matching.

description: Actual timestamp when the paint stage was completed and the vehicle body was released to the trim/general assembly line. Null if stage not yet completed.
